desc: Trace why file gone (deleted or renamed). Uses Linux eBPF/bcc.
r: filegone - Trace why file gone (deleted or renamed). Uses Linux eBPF/bcc.

This traces why file gone/vanished, providing information on who deleted or renamed the file.

This works by tracing the kernel vfs_unlink() , vfs_rmdir() , vfs_rename functions.

Since this uses BPF, only the root user can use this tool.
<dl><dt data-o="">-h</dt><dd>Print usage message.</dd><dt data-o="">-p PID</dt><dd>Trace this process ID only (filtered in-kernel).</dd></dl>

Trace all file gone events
# filegone
Trace file gone events caused by PID 181:
# filegone -p 181

<dl><dt>TIME</dt><dd>Time of the event.</dd><dt>PID</dt><dd>Process ID that renamed/deleted the file.</dd><dt>COMM</dt><dd>Process name for the PID.</dd><dt>ACTION</dt><dd>action on file: 'DELETE' or 'RENAME'</dd><dt>FILE</dt><dd>Filename.</dd></dl>

This traces the kernel VFS file rename and delete functions and prints output for each event. As the rate of this is generally expected to be low (< 1000/s), the overhead is also expected to be negligible. This is from bcc.

https://github.com/iovisor/bcc

Also look in the bcc distribution for a companion _examples.txt file containing example usage, output, and commentary for this tool.
